800: Stay close to good people who have no faults. Leave the friendship of unworthy people, even if it costs you something to get away.
806: People who keep to the rules of true friendship will not leave old friends, even when that friendship causes them loss.
821: The friendship of people who spend time with you but are not with you in heart is like an anvil, the iron block a blacksmith hammers on. When they get the chance, they will strike you down on it.
824: Be afraid of two-faced people who smile sweetly with their faces while their hearts mean you harm.
837: When a fool becomes very rich, strangers eat their fill while the fool's own family goes hungry.
840: A fool walking into a gathering of good and worthy people is like putting unwashed feet on a clean bed.
847: A fool who does not keep good advice, or lets an important secret slip, does great harm to themselves.
851: Hostility (the wish to fight and oppose others) is called a disease. In every living being, it spreads the bad habit of not getting along with others.
852: Even if someone who wants to break away from you does things that hurt you, the best thing is not to hurt them back out of hostility.
853: If you get rid of the painful disease called hostility, you will win a spotless fame that never fades.
854: When hostility, the worst of all pains, is gone, the greatest of all joys comes.
855: Who could ever beat people who can turn away from hostility whenever it rises inside them?
858: Turning away from hostility brings good things. If you push it further, harm comes rushing toward you.
859: When good times are coming, a person does not even look at hostility. When harm is coming to them, they try to make their hostility bigger.
860: All painful things come from hostility. Friendliness brings the proud joy of true goodness.
863: A person who is fearful, does not know what they should know, cannot get along with others, and will not give is very easy for enemies to beat.
870: A person who will not take even the small, easy win of fighting an enemy with no learning will never become famous.
871: Being enemies with others has nothing good in it. No one should want it, not even as a game or a joke.
872: Even if you make enemies of soldiers who use the bow as their plow, never make enemies of learned people who use words as their plow.
874: The world holds together because of the greatness of a person of good character who makes enemies into friends and lives that way.
884: If hidden hostility grows from a mind that is not good, it brings many troubles and turns a person's own people against them.
885: If hidden hostility grows among relatives, it brings many deadly troubles.
886: Once people who were united start to split apart, it is always hard for them to escape being destroyed.
887: A family with hidden hostility inside may look joined together like a box and its lid, but it is never truly united.
888: A family with hostility inside wears itself down and loses its strength, like metal worn away by a file.
889: Even if hostility inside a group is as small as half a sesame seed, ruin is hiding inside it.
901: Men who are ruled by desire for their wives miss the greatest reward in life. People who want to get real work done stay away from this very habit.
909: Men who simply do whatever their wives command will have no good deeds, no real riches, and none of life's other joys either.
910: People whose minds are full of careful thought and who are strong inside will never fall into the foolishness of being ruled by a woman.
923: Being drunk is painful to see even for the mother who gave birth to you. How much worse must it look to good and wise people?
924: The good lady called Shame (the feeling that stops us from doing wrong) turns her back on those who commit the great wrong of drinking, a wrong no one should welcome.
930: When a drinker is sober and sees someone else who is drunk, do they not think that they look just as bad when they drink?
